opener.seg: [Translation of paragraph of an article from the newspaper La Tribuna of September 17, 1883.]

div.p: Such being the state of affairs, it came to the knowledge of Commander Gonzales, chief of the forces for the restoration of peace, that Chiclayo and Lambayeque were about to be sacked, and that there were neutral interests there that demanded his protection. He thereupon reoccupied Chiclayo, assembled the gamonales and the principal instigators of the anarchy in which they want to keep the place, and of whom there met seventy-two, and asked them where were the constituted authorities? They replied that in San Pedro. Why? Because the montaneros had driven them away. And the urban guard, and you, why did you not defend them? Because you do not desire peace, and therefore jeopardize so “much valuable property. To this Drs. Chacaltana, Arbulu, and Iagle replied that they were desirous of peace, but with Dr. Garcia Calderon.

Commander Gonzales thereupon ordered the imprisonment of those gentlemen, and moreover levied a contribution of 50,000 silver soles and 200 rifles, payable in twenty-four hours, under threat of suffering the penalties in consequence of their disobedience. You can hardly imagine the chagrin of the seventy-two as they left, and, immediately reassembling, they drew out the record of adhesion and submission to General Iglesias.
